faq.q: Why are 1% Lows and 0.1% Lows more important than Average FPS?
faq.a: Average FPS masks intermittent stutter. A game running at 100 FPS average can still feel choppy if sudden 50ms frame delivery stalls occur. 1% and 0.1% lows measure the worst 1% and 0.1% of frame delivery times, directly reflecting perceptual smoothness.

faq.q: Which benchmarking utilities produce compatible CSV files?
faq.a: The analyzer automatically identifies headers from Intel PresentMon, CapFrameX, MSI Afterburner / RivaTuner (RTSS), and Fraps CSV outputs.

faq.q: What is considered a micro-stutter in this tool?
faq.a: A frame delivery interval that exceeds 2.5 times the run mean frame time is classified as an anomalous stutter event.

faq.q: Are my hardware benchmark files uploaded to any server?
faq.a: No. All statistical sorting, percentile evaluations, and SVG graph rendering execute entirely inside your local browser memory.

articleHtml:
Engineering Science of Frame Pacing and Micro-Stutter

In graphics engineering and PC gaming performance evaluation, Average Frames Per Second (FPS) is an insufficient metric for evaluating real-world visual fluidity. A system delivering an average of 120 FPS can still exhibit severe perceptible hitching and input lag if frames are delivered irregularly. Frame pacing—the consistency of milliseconds elapsed between consecutive image presentations—determines perceived smoothness.

When assessing game engines or GPU architectures, modern benchmarking tools such as Intel PresentMon and CapFrameX record the exact duration of each frame presentation call (msBetweenPresents). By analyzing the distribution curve of these intervals, engineers isolate hardware bottlenecks, driver shader compilation stalls, and thermal throttling events.

Diagnostic Percentile Standards

  • Average Frame Time (ms): Represents the mathematical mean of all captured intervals. For 60 Hz displays, the target frame time is 16.66 ms; for 144 Hz displays, 6.94 ms; for 240 Hz displays, 4.16 ms.
  • 1% Low FPS (99th Percentile Duration): Measures the performance of the slowest 1% of frames during the run. A large gap between Average FPS and 1% Low indicates frame pacing instability or CPU thread contention.
  • 0.1% Low FPS (99.9th Percentile Duration): Captures severe hitching events, asset streaming stutters, and garbage collection pauses that disrupt gameplay immersion.

Air-Gapped Client-Side Data Evaluation

Competitive esports analysts and hardware reviewers often log proprietary gameplay sessions and pre-release hardware benchmarks. By calculating all statistics and generating SVG graphs within local browser memory, Toolkit Gen ensures your hardware telemetry and system benchmarks are never shared with remote entities.

Statistical Foundations of Frame Pacing Analysis

Evaluating graphics engine performance requires rigorous statistical analysis of frame presentation intervals. While casual performance benchmarking relies on arithmetic mean FPS (Frames Per Second), arithmetic means fail to capture transient stutter events. For example, a benchmark run averaging 120 FPS can deliver 119 frames in 500 ms followed by a single catastrophic 500 ms frame freeze; the arithmetic mean registers a deceptively smooth score, while the human visual cortex perceives an intolerable jarring hitch.

PresentMon and CapFrameX capture raw frame intervals (msBetweenPresents). By sorting these intervals in ascending order, we compute non-parametric percentile ranks. The 99th percentile frame delivery duration represents the 1% Low frame time, while the 99.9th percentile duration represents the 0.1% Low frame time. Converting these durations back into instantaneous FPS provides an accurate representation of minimum perceived smoothness.

Diagnostic Performance Ratio Benchmarks

Pacing Stability Metric Formula / Ratio Diagnostic Evaluation
Excellent Pacing 1% Low >= 80% of Avg FPS Near-perfect frame delivery; optimal GPU utilization
Moderate Stutter 1% Low between 50% - 79% Occasional asset streaming or shader compilation stalls
Severe Hitching 1% Low < 50% of Avg FPS CPU thread bottlenecks, thermal throttling, or RAM paging

Hardware Reviewer Privacy Standards

Hardware journalists and benchmarking laboratories frequently evaluate confidential pre-release GPU architectures and unreleased game titles under strict non-disclosure agreements (NDAs). Toolkit Gen calculates all percentile distributions, frame variance metrics, and SVG interactive graphs strictly in browser memory without sending telemetry to remote analytical databases.
